title: Minimum Cost to Move Chips to The Same Position
spaceBreakdown:
- int oddCount: single integer → O(1)
- int evenCount: single integer → O(1)
- not counted: input vector
approach: Moving a chip by ±2 is free, so any chip can reach any position of the same parity at no cost. Moving by ±1 costs 1 and flips parity. Therefore, all chips at odd positions can gather at any odd position for free, and all chips at even positions can gather at any even position for free. To unify everyone, we either move all odd-parity chips to an even position (cost = number of odd-position chips) or all even-parity chips to an odd position (cost = number of even-position chips). The answer is the smaller of these two counts.
hints: Since moving a chip by ±2 costs nothing, what property of a position is preserved no matter how many free moves you make?
Count chips by parity (odd vs even position). For [1,2,3]: positions 1 and 3 are odd (count 2), position 2 is even (count 1). The answer is min(2, 1) = 1.

```
odd = 0, even = 0
for each position p:
    if p is even: even = even + 1
    else: odd = odd + 1
return min(odd, even)
```

**Single chip** - only one chip exists, no moves needed
`Input: position = [5]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: returning max(oddCount, evenCount) instead of min → returns 1

**All same parity** - every chip already shares the same parity, cost is zero
`Input: position = [2,4,6,8]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: returning oddCount + evenCount instead of min → returns 4

**Equal split** - odd and even counts are equal, either direction costs the same
`Input: position = [1,2]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: returning abs(oddCount - evenCount) instead of min → returns 0

**All chips at same position** - duplicates at one spot, already gathered
`Input: position = [3,3,3,3]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: returning position.size() as the cost → returns 4

followUps.q: What if moving by ±2 costs 1 and moving by ±1 costs 2?
followUps.a: The free-move advantage disappears, so parity alone no longer determines cost. We would try each unique position as the target and compute the total cost as the sum of floor(|p−t|/2) + 2×(|p−t| mod 2) over all chips. TC: O(n²), SC: O(1).

followUps.q: What if n can be up to 10^5 instead of 100?
followUps.a: The parity-counting solution already runs in O(n) and uses O(1) space, so it handles 10^5 chips with no change. We only count odd vs even positions in a single pass; the position values themselves are irrelevant.

followUps.q: What if chips can only move right (position+1 or position+2)?
followUps.a: The target must be at or beyond the rightmost chip, so its parity is fixed to max(position)'s parity. Every chip with the opposite parity pays exactly 1; same-parity chips pay 0. Cost = count of chips whose parity differs from max(position). TC: O(n), SC: O(1).
